title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: GAR — Gen 2:17 threat fulfilled as judge?
pass_a_gloss: GAR next asks how Placeus can say the first man's fall needed no judicial action of God. While man was still integral God set the law not to taste the forbidden fruit with the grave threat dying you shall die (Gen. 2:17). God fulfilled that threat as judge—stripping gifts and plunging into miseries—so here too nothing is unlike the courtier who needs a judge's act.
pass_b_english: GAR. Next, how is it said that in what befell the first man there was no need of God's judicial action? Had not God, while man was still integral, proposed a law of not tasting the forbidden fruit, with the most grave threat added that if he did otherwise he would die the death, Gen. 2:17? Which threat God fulfilled, and fulfilled as judge, and therefore in stripping man of his gifts and plunging him into various miseries exercised a judicial action? Here too there is nothing unlike.
source_text: GAR. Deinde, quomodo dicitur in iis quae acciderunt primo homini, nulla opus fuisse judiciaria Dei actione? Annon homini adhuc integro legem Deus proposuerat, de non gustando fructu interdicto, addita gravissima comminatione, si secus faceret, morte moriturum, Gen. 2. 17. Quam comminationem Deus adimplevit, & adimplevit ut judex, ac proinde in spoliando homine suis donis, & in varias miserias demergendo judiciariam actionem exercuit? Hic quoque nihil dissimile.
